title: Semantic Tokens
summary: Extend existing semantic references into registered text and media projections while keeping authoring, rendering, and usage review inside Docs Viewer.
content_html:
Semantic Tokens

Purpose

Extend the shipped semantic-reference path so a registered work, tag, asset, or later supported object can be projected as ordinary text or media while retaining its stable identity and queryable relationships.

The main implementation outcome is a durable, extensible registry and JSON contract. Editor assistance and reports should remain small, focused projections of that data rather than defining its complete shape.

This is planning direction, not implementation approval.

Product Contract

A semantic token is an authored reference to a registered target plus a permitted projection. The rendered result may look like an ordinary link or image, but its source retains structured intent.

registered target
    -> Add token assistance in the Docs Viewer source editor
    -> source token
    -> builder resolution
    -> ordinary rendered HTML + generated usage JSON
    -> Docs Viewer report and future JSON consumers

A manually authored Markdown link remains valid, but it carries only its literal label and URL. A semantic token identifies the target, follows target-kind rules, and can be reported without searching document prose.

Registry Contract First

The canonical and generated JSON must be designed before widening the UI. The contract should provide:

  • a schema-versioned envelope and stable target identities;
  • a small required core for target kind, title, ownership, and current representation or destination identity;
  • typed optional metadata and registered-target relationships without making every conceivable field mandatory;
  • room for media representations or variants without making provider paths the semantic identity;
  • generated target lookup and relationship projections kept separate from canonical records and reproducible from them.

Consumers should request or derive the focused projection they need. A report does not need to display every registry field merely because the field is available to another report, build, or future consumer.

One Docs Viewer Surface

Keep the existing composition:

  • the Docs Viewer source editor owns authoring and the local source buffer;
  • the Info panel searches registered targets and assists token insertion;
  • the builder resolves supported projections and emits relationship artifacts;
  • Docs Viewer reports reconcile registered targets, stored bytes, document usage, stale targets, and related data.

Do not create a separate route, asset portal, or management application for this workflow.

Targets And Projections

Canonical records remain with their domain owners. The semantic-token layer provides common identity, projection, insertion, rendering, and relationship contracts.

target example projections example destinations
Studio work title, representative image work page, associated Analysis document
Studio tag title tag document in the configured Analysis sub-scope
Scope asset title, image, download asset bytes, associated describing document

The semantic-reference registry declares supported kinds and their capabilities; it does not become the canonical store for every target record.

Registered Assets

A scope asset needs a stable identity independent of its filename, storage provider, or current served URL. A scope-owned JSON registry should hold the canonical record, including the published object identity, a small stable core, and optional typed metadata and relationships. The registry schema should make future metadata possible without preloading the first UI or report with fields that have no current use.

Every media object added through the source-editor UI should be registered automatically. Registration is not an optional authoring choice:

  • Add image/file publishes and verifies the bytes, creates the asset record, then inserts its semantic token;
  • Insert existing asset searches registered assets and inserts another token for the selected identity.

If an author abandons the document edit after adding media, the result is a valid registered but unused asset rather than unregistered bytes.

Document usage is derived from tokens rather than maintained manually in the asset record:

document -> embeds -> asset -> tagged-with -> tag:randomness

Storage inspection remains useful for reconciliation: registered bytes may be available or missing, and bytes may exist without a registered record. It is not the authority for deciding which assets exist as registered data objects.

Focused Media Report

The intended steady state is complete registration:

  • every stored scope media object has one registered asset identity;
  • every displayed document usage refers to that identity through a semantic token rather than a manually authored path or link.

One focused built-in Docs Viewer report should join the scope asset registry, configured filesystem or R2 inventory, and generated document-usage JSON. This supports registration progress and practical troubleshooting; it is not the primary authority or a general runtime health system.

registered asset stored bytes document usage report meaning
yes yes semantic token fully registered usage
yes yes none registered but unused
yes yes raw path or link registered asset with unstructured usage
no yes raw path or link used but unregistered media
no yes none unregistered stored media
yes no token or none registered asset with missing bytes
missing target unknown semantic token dangling semantic relationship

Unused is not independently an error. The first report should show only the identity, registration, availability, and usage fields needed for this reconciliation, with focused filters such as Unregistered, Raw references, Missing bytes, and Unused. Tag- or metadata-specific reports can read the same JSON later without widening this report.

Work Needed

  • [ ] Define the canonical registry envelope and target-record schema first: immutable identity, target kind, ownership, title, representations, optional typed metadata, relationships, and schema evolution.
  • [ ] Define which JSON is canonical, generated, local-only, or safe for future consumers, and keep derived document usage out of canonical target records.
  • [ ] Define one source-token contract for target kind, stable id, projection, destination, and occurrence-specific presentation data.
  • [ ] Extend the semantic kind registry with declared target-source, projection, and destination capabilities without hardcoding kinds in route or editor controllers.
  • [ ] Add focused target-source adapters for tags and assets, then include their safe records in the generated target lookup used by the Info panel.
  • [ ] Extend source-editor assistance to select an existing registered asset or automatically register newly added media before inserting its token. Registration must not become an optional checkbox. Keep source writes and rebuilds in the existing editor workflow.
  • [ ] Extend builder resolution beyond text links to supported text, image, and file projections while preserving typed rendering and sanitization rules.
  • [ ] Emit stable generated JSON for document-to-target and target-to-target relationships, with an explicit missing or stale target policy.
  • [ ] Add one Docs Viewer media report that reconciles registry records, stored bytes, semantic-token usage, and transitional raw references, then supports the smallest useful registration and usage filters.
  • [ ] Reconcile existing path-based media tokens and unregistered stored bytes, and plan any migration without retaining two permanent media identities.
  • [ ] Prove the JSON contracts, target resolution, source-editor integration, and focused report inputs without building an exhaustive runtime audit or validation matrix.

Boundaries

  • No separate semantic-token or asset-management route.
  • No generic graph database, background crawler, or content-search dependency.
  • No background registry-health process or broad runtime reconciliation regime.
  • No universal report that exposes every available metadata field.
  • No central replacement for the canonical Studio work, tag, document, or scope-asset owners.
  • The Docs service may enforce JSON parseability, required identity fields, and safe reads or writes, but it surfaces registry data rather than judging its semantic completeness or continuously validating cross-record truth.
  • No guarantee that a target exists forever; insertion confirms current availability, while generated reports expose later drift.
  • No new projection becomes a registry entry alone: its target source, builder resolver, editor assistance, generated relationship data, and report behavior must be accepted together.

The existing Semantic References Editor is the working text-link baseline. Scope Media Management should be reshaped around registered assets rather than physical inventory before an asset delivery is promoted.
